title: Biden to announce $147 million for clean energy upgrades to Port of Baltimore
summary: President Joe Biden (D) will announce $3 billion in environmental grants to support efforts in reducing emissions at ports in 27 states, including $147 million for Port of Baltimore during a visit Tuesday to the Dundalk Marine Terminal.
content:
by Danielle J. Brown, Maryland Matters October 29, 2024

by Danielle J. Brown, Maryland Matters October 29, 2024

President Joe Biden (D) will announce $3 billion in environmental grants to support efforts in reducing emissions at ports in 27 states, including $147 million for Port of Baltimore during a visit Tuesday to the Dundalk Marine Terminal.

The Maryland Port Association will receive more than $145 million for the Port of Baltimore to purchase zero-emission cargo handling equipment and drayage trucks, as well as other expenses to reduce pollution produced by the port, according to the administration. An additional $2 million will go toward planning to further reduce emissions, according to a statement from the White House.

The Biden administration says the funding announced Tuesday will help support up to 2,000 union jobs at the port.

The announcement comes less than a month after members of the International Longshoremen’s Association staged a short-lived strike after contract negotiations fell through with the U.S. Maritime Alliance, which represents shipping companies, and the union’s previous contract expired on Oct. 1. That strike involved 45,000 dockworkers at ports from Maine to Texas, including Baltimore.

The walkout ended two days later after the two sides agreed on higher wages and, under pressure from the Biden administration, agreed to extend the previous contract through Jan. 15 to continue negotiations or remaining issues, primarily a union demand to prohibit automation of union jobs on the docks.

Gov. Wes Moore (D) is scheduled to attend Tuesday afternoon’s event with the president, along with “Maryland congressional leadership, and other Biden Administration officials in Baltimore,” according to the governor’s office.

The federal funding comes from the Environmental Protection Agency’s Clean Ports grants program, a feature of the Inflation Reduction Act, which will distribute $3 billion to 55 grantees across 27 states and territories. Funds will go toward upgrading port operations and infrastructure to cleaner equipment. The grants are expected to support up to 40,000 jobs, both inside and outside the ports, according to the administration.

With just one week out from the election, Biden could touch on a few campaign points in favor of Vice President Kamala Harris’s presidential run and may also provide an comments on efforts to secure full federal funding to replace Key Bridge. But the Clean Ports grant funding is scheduled to be the focal point of the event.
